sections.h2: What are my main options for selling a house in Lauderdale Lakes?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. Each route trades speed against price and effort, so match it to what is wrong with the property and how soon you need to close.

Lauderdale Lakes sits in Broward County, and the county offices (property appraiser, tax collector, clerk of the circuit court) handle the paperwork that follows any sale here. The city runs its own website for local services, and it was promoting a Business Growth Initiative pitch competition for local entrepreneurs in late 2026, a sign of how the city is trying to build up its commercial side.

  • A listing suits a house in good shape with time to show it.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale saves the agent's share but leaves contracts, disclosures and paperwork to you.
  • A cash purchase suits a house with deferred repairs, tenants, liens or a deadline.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work when the house has tenants in it?
sections.html:
A tenant does not have to leave just because you sign a sale contract, so plan the buyer's timeline around the lease and Florida's notice rules. A buyer who purchases with the tenant in place avoids the notice process, while a buyer who wants the house empty needs the lease ended first.

Florida's landlord and tenant statute sets the clocks. For unpaid rent, the notice runs 3 days, not counting Saturdays, Sundays or court holidays (s. 83.56). A curable lease breach gives the tenant 7 days to fix it, and a breach that cannot be fixed gives 7 days to leave. Month-to-month tenancies end on at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period, and year-to-year tenancies need 60 days (s. 83.57).

The notice can be mailed, handed over, e-mailed under s. 83.505, or left at the home if the tenant is away, and a lease cannot waive these requirements. If the tenant contests the case beyond a payment defense, the tenant must deposit the rent claimed into the court registry within 5 days, again excluding weekends and holidays, or lose the defenses (s. 83.60). After a judgment, the sheriff acts on the clerk's writ after 24 hours' posted notice (s. 83.62).

  • Ask the buyer in writing whether they will take the house subject to the lease.
  • Give the tenant's rent history and deposit details to the closing agent.
  • Keep copies of every notice you deliver and how you delivered it.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and recording charges come with a Lauderdale Lakes sale?
sections.html:
The main transfer cost is the documentary stamp tax on the deed, set at 70 cents per $100 of consideration for every county except Miami-Dade (s. 201.02, s. 201.031). Broward falls under the 70 cent rate. Consideration counts money, discharged debts, and any mortgage on the property whether or not the buyer assumes it.

The Department of Revenue states that all parties to the document are liable regardless of which side agrees to pay, so the contract should name who covers it. The Broward clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Recording itself carries clerk charges under s. 28.24: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 per added page, plus the records modernization fee and a per-page technology charge.

Ask the closing agent for a written estimate of both lines before you sign, so the doc stamp figure and recording fee appear in your net sheet.

sections.h2: How do Broward property taxes affect my closing?
sections.html:
Florida taxes are assessed as of January 1, billed in November, and paid in arrears, so the seller's share for the months owned is settled at closing. The Broward County Property Appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, and its office can be reached at 954-357-6830 on weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm.

A sale ends the homestead cap benefit. Under Save Our Homes, a homestead's assessed value rises by the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change each year, but a change of ownership resets the next owner's assessment to just value on the following January 1 (s. 193.155). Expect the buyer's first bill to be higher than yours, and say so if you are asked.

Property tax dates printed by the Florida Department of Revenue
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed
25 days after the noticePetition window for a value challenge
NovemberTax bills mailed
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent

The early-payment discount is printed as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.

sections.h2: What if my Lauderdale Lakes house is vacant or in poor repair?
sections.html:
A vacant or worn house still sells, but the price and buyer pool change. Lenders and conventional buyers often balk at deferred repairs, while a cash buyer prices the work and closes without an inspection-driven renegotiation.

Homestead status has a side effect here. Florida says homestead is lost if the home is rented, stops being your permanent residence, or you cease to be a Florida resident, and the exemption must be claimed by March 1 on Form DR-501. If you moved out and still hold a homestead exemption, tell the property appraiser rather than letting the roll carry it.

  • Walk the property and list defects before you accept any offer.
  • Check the Broward tax collector for unpaid balances.
  • Ask the title company about liens that could delay closing.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on payments and worried about foreclosure?
sections.html:
Florida foreclosures are judicial, so a lender must win a court judgment before a sale, and you often have time to sell first. After judgment, the clerk sets a public sale 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to longer (s. 45.031).

Notice of sale is published for two consecutive weeks. The winning bidder posts 5 percent of the bid, and if no one objects within 10 days of the certificate of sale, the sale is confirmed. A sale before judgment by you avoids that path, and any surplus from a foreclosure sale can be claimed through the clerk, who should be asked within 10 days of the sale if the home was your homestead.

Talk to your servicer and the closing agent about a payoff statement, and ask whether a short sale or a cash close fits your balance.

faqs.q: What is the documentary stamp tax on a deed in Lauderdale Lakes?
faqs.a: It is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, because Lauderdale Lakes is in Broward, not Miami-Dade (s. 201.02). All parties to the deed are liable, so your contract should say who pays. The clerk collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell while a tenant lives in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease stays in force, so a buyer either takes the house with the tenant or waits for a lawful notice process to end the tenancy. Nonpayment notices run 3 days, and month-to-month tenancies need 30 days' notice (s. 83.56, s. 83.57).

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property returns to just value the following January 1 (s. 193.155). You may be able to carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old homestead.

faqs.q: When are Broward property tax bills mailed, and when are they late?
faqs.a: Bills go out in November and unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1. Ask the Broward tax collector for the exact balance before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need probate before selling an inherited Lauderdale Lakes home?
faqs.a: Usually yes, unless the estate qualifies for summary administration, which applies when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less or the owner died more than two years ago (s. 735.201). A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable for doc stamps.
